nodes.title: Strict formal modules, O-displays and relative duality
nodes.statement: Let O be the ring of integers of a finite extension of ℚ_p, with uniformizer π. Over an O-algebra R in which π is nilpotent, a strict O-module is a p-divisible group X with an action ι:O→End(X) through which O acts on Lie X by the structure map O→R; it is formal when X is a formal group. An O-display over R is a window over the Witt O-frame (W_O(R),I_O(R),F,V) of relative O-Witt vectors with respect to π, and strict formal O-modules over R are equivalent to nilpotent O-displays, compatibly with base change; the relative height of X is the rank of its O-display P and its dimension is the rank of P/Q. A strict formal O-module is biformal when its dual O-display is again nilpotent; its relative dual X^∨ is the strict O-module of that dual display, and it depends on π. A polarization (resp. principal polarization) is an isogeny (resp. isomorphism) λ:X→X^∨ with λ^∨=−λ. The relative crystal D_X on O-divided-power thickenings carries the Hodge filtration; deformations along such thickenings correspond to lifts of the filtration, and for principally polarized biformal X to Lagrangian lifts for the perfect alternating pairing on D_X. For a finite totally ramified extension O⊂O′, strict formal O′-modules are equivalent to nilpotent windows over the Lubin–Tate O′-frame, compatibly with duality after rescaling the pairing by a unit of the frame.
hypotheses: O, π as stated; R an O-algebra in which π is nilpotent; duality and polarizations only for biformal objects.
proofSteps: Define relative O-Witt vectors with respect to π, the Witt O-frame and its windows (Mih19 Definition 11.7).

Deduce the equivalence of strict formal O-modules with nilpotent O-displays from the equivalence between nilpotent displays and formal p-divisible groups (gap:zink-display-equivalence) by the Ahsendorf–Cheng–Zink construction recalled in Mih19 §11.2.

Define duals of biformal objects through the dual window, polarizations by λ^∨=−λ, and the relative crystal and Hodge filtration (Mih19 Definitions 11.6, 11.9 and §11.2); prove the Lubin–Tate frame equivalence and its duality compatibility (Mih19 Proposition 12.11 and Lemma 11.2).

nodes.title: Representability of the unitary framed functors
nodes.statement: For local PEL data in the sense of RZ96 Definition 3.21 (a semisimple ℚ_p-algebra B with involution, a maximal order O_B, a self-dual periodic multichain 𝓛 of O_B-lattices, a cocharacter with local reflex field E and a framing object over F̄_p), the functor 𝓜 on schemes over Spf O_Ĕ on which p is locally nilpotent, of 𝓛-sets of p-divisible groups with O_B-action satisfying the Kottwitz condition, with the polarizations prescribed by 𝓛 and a framing quasi-isogeny over the special fibre, is represented by a formal scheme locally formally of finite type over Spf O_Ĕ. Consequently the functors N_n of U1, N¹_n of U2, N^exo of U3 and N_n^Kra of U5 are represented by separated formal schemes locally formally of finite type over Spf O_L̆ in every case (O_L̆=O_K̆ when L/K is unramified): each is, for suitable data, the closed formal subscheme of such an 𝓜 cut out by the strictness of U0, the Eisenstein conditions, the relative polarization and kernel conditions, the wedge condition, and the open and closed conditions of height zero and exact multiplier; N^exo is moreover intersected with the open spin locus, and N_n^Kra is the closed subscheme of the relative Grassmannian of rank-(n−1) summands of Lie X cut out by the Krämer conditions. The space Ñ_n of U2 is closed in N¹_n×N_{n+1}. None of these formal schemes is asserted to be quasi-compact or to carry the p-adic topology.
hypotheses: p>2 for the unitary consequences; the data of RZ96 Definition 3.21 for the general statement.
proofSteps: Represent the unstructured functor of framed p-divisible groups (RZ96 Theorem 2.16) and cut out the O_B-stable locus and the 𝓛-set conditions as closed subfunctors; the Kottwitz condition is closed (RZ96 proof of Theorem 3.25).

Translate the relative conditions of U0 (strict action, relative polarization of U0/strict-module-display) into closed conditions on the absolute p-divisible group, and the height and multiplier conditions into open and closed ones.
Add the Krämer filtration as a closed subscheme of a Grassmannian bundle and the spin condition as an open condition; separatedness follows from rigidity of quasi-isogenies.
acceptance: At n=1 with L/K unramified, N_1=Spf O_L̆ (LZ22 §2.2): the strict O_L-action leaves no deformation parameter, whereas the unstructured deformation space of the underlying p-divisible group, of height 2[K:ℚ_p] and dimension [K:ℚ_p], has [K:ℚ_p]² parameters.
The spin condition is open, not closed: imposing only the closed conditions on the exotic functor adds the locus where i(u) acts by zero on Lie at some geometric point.
At n=2 the completed local ring of N_2 at a point is O_L̆[[t]], whose ideal of definition contains t; the topology is not the p-adic one.

IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration §IG.0.27 is the case of an unramified datum with a single self-dual lattice; the almost self-dual chain Λ⊂Λ^♯ of U2, with Λ^♯/Λ of length one, and the ramified data of U3 and U5 lie outside it.

nodes.title: Strict polarized unitary modules
nodes.statement: For a quadratic extension L/K of p-adic fields with p odd, fix an embedding L into the completed maximal unramified extension L̆. A principal hermitian O_L-module of signature (r,s), r+s=n>0, is a strict formal O_K-module X of relative K-height 2n and dimension n, with O_L-action i and principal relative polarization λ satisfying λ i(a)=i(ā)^∨ λ and det(T−i(a)|Lie X)=(T−a)^r(T−ā)^s for every a∈O_L. nodes.title: Mihatsch relative comparison
nodes.statement: Suppose L/K is unramified quadratic and ℚ_p⊂K₀⊂K. On locally noetherian nilpotent bases, construct Mihatsch’s equivalence C from supersingular hermitian O_L–O_K₀-modules with signature P(r,s) and its structural-action Eisenstein clause to supersingular strict O_K hermitian O_L-modules of signature (r,s). For K/K₀ unramified, contract the embedding-graded display by a full Frobenius round trip. For K/K₀ totally ramified, lift the pairing through the inverse-different trace, pass through the Lubin–Tate frame and rescale by the frame-change unit. Compose along the unramified/totally ramified factorization. C is compatible with Rosati adjoints and polarized quasi-isogenies. Write Ψ for the K₀-embeddings of the maximal subfield Lᵘ⊂L unramified over K₀, split into conjugate halves Ψ₀,Ψ₁ with distinguished ψ₀∈Ψ₀. Put P₀₁(a;T)=∏_{ψ∈Ψ₁}ψ(charpoly_{L/Lᵘ}(a;T)), P₁₀=P₀₁(T−a)/(T−ā), and P(r,s)=P₁₀^r P₀₁^s; the indicated quotient is polynomial. Require this characteristic polynomial on Lie and (i(a)−a)|Lie_{ψ₀}=0 for every a∈O_L. This last zero-endomorphism equation is part of the input. On the O_K₀ side the relative height and dimension are 2n[K:K₀] and n[K:K₀]; the strict O_K side has height 2n and dimension n.
proofSteps: Use the O-display and Lubin–Tate window equivalences of U0/strict-module-display and normal decompositions.
In the totally ramified case keep the inverse-different generator and the unit correcting the change of frame.
Identify contracted Hodge crystals and homomorphism lifting across square-zero thickenings, then induct along the nilpotent nilradical of a noetherian base.
acceptance: The comparison applies when K/ℚ_p is ramified; this is distinct from the exotic comparison in U4.
On the relative side the height is 2n, not the absolute height.

nodes.title: Exotic connected components
nodes.statement: Let K/ℚ_p be finite with p>2, L/K ramified quadratic, n even with n≥2, and N^exo the relative exotic framed space of U3/exotic-rz. Then N^exo has exactly two connected components: the loci where the parity invariant κ₂(ρ)=ht(ρ₁) mod 2 of the minimal cover (X̃,ρ₁,ρ₂) of the height-zero framing ρ is 0, respectively 1. The reduced locus of each component is connected and is the union of closed Bruhat–Tits strata V_Λ indexed by the vertex lattices Λ of V^exo; each V_Λ meets each component in a nonempty connected smooth projective variety of dimension t(Λ)/2−1, V_Λ∩V_Λ′ is V_{Λ+Λ′} or empty according as Λ+Λ′ is a vertex lattice or not, and the irreducible components are the V_Λ of maximal type t(Λ)=n. In particular each component of N^exo_red has pure dimension n/2−1.
hypotheses: L/K ramified quadratic, p>2, u a uniformizer of L with ū=−u, n even and n≥2; strict relative O_K-module conventions as in U0; K/ℚ_p an arbitrary finite extension.
proofSteps: Define κ₂ by the minimal cover of the framing; it is locally constant, so the two loci are open and closed (Wu16 §3.4).

Construct the Bruhat–Tits stratification over K by the special-Hom lattices of U3/exotic-special-hom and identify each closed stratum with the generalized Deligne–Lusztig variety of the orthogonal group of Λ^∨/Λ over the residue field (LL22 Proposition 2.28).

Every vertex lattice lies in one of maximal type and the simplicial complex of vertex lattices is connected; hence each κ₂-locus has connected reduced locus (the argument of Wu16 Theorem 5.18(2), which uses only the hermitian lattice combinatorics of L/K and so applies over every K, as LL22 footnote 8 records).
Both loci are nonempty, since every stratum V_Λ meets each of them (LL22 Proposition 2.28(2)); a framing self-quasi-isogeny g with κ₂(g)=1 maps one isomorphically onto the other (Wu16 (3.24)).
acceptance: At K=ℚ_p and n=2 there are two components, each formally smooth of relative dimension 1, with reduced locus of dimension n/2−1=0; reading the dimension of the reduced locus as the relative dimension would give 1.

At n=2 the space V^exo is two-dimensional and nonsplit, hence anisotropic; every vertex lattice has type 2, no two distinct vertex lattices span a vertex lattice, and connectedness forces the reduced locus of each component to be a single point.
The labels depend on the framing, not on the geometry of one component: a framing self-quasi-isogeny g exchanges the two components when κ₂(g)=1 and preserves each when κ₂(g)=0 (Wu16 (3.24)).

nodes.title: Krämer normal-crossing charts
nodes.statement: Over the natural ramified coefficient DVR with p odd, the principal Krämer local-model charts meeting the exceptional locus have equation y(Σ_{i=1}^n x_i²)=2u with x_k=1, for some k. At an intersection point the residue quadric Σx_i²=0 is smooth, so this is étale locally yz=u times n−2 smooth parameters. For n≥3 this is the chart in Krämer03 (4.11). For n=2 the same equations give y(1+x²)=2u; at either geometric root of 1+x² the derivative 2x is invertible, giving the same crossing chart. This rank-two extension asserts local normal crossings and does not assert the global irreducibility of the n≥3 quadric.
proofSteps: Choose the invertible Hodge minor and normalize the kth coordinate of the extra line.
Eliminate the symmetric matrix A and γ using A+uI=λγᵗ and λ_k=1 to obtain yΣx_i²=2u.
At quadric points use its nonzero gradient for an étale coordinate z=Σx_i²/2; away the quadric or y=0 use the smooth equation.
For n=2 check the two geometric roots explicitly, without importing the n≥3 geometric irreducibility assertion.
acceptance: The n=2 crossing is étale locally yz=u over O_L̆.
The n=2 residue quadric consists of two geometric points, so it is not claimed irreducible.
The chart after u=t^e with e>1 need not be regular.

nodes.title: Integral CM moduli at every prime
nodes.statement: Let F/F⁺ be a CM field, Φ a CM type with reflex field E_Φ, and a a fractional ideal of F⁺. The moduli problem M₀^a over O_{E_Φ} of triples (A₀,ι₀,λ₀), with A₀ an abelian scheme, ι₀:O_F→End(A₀) satisfying the Kottwitz condition char(ι₀(a)|Lie A₀)=∏_{φ∈Φ}(T−φ(a)) for all a∈O_F, and λ₀ a polarization of type a whose Rosati involution induces conjugation on O_F, is a Deligne–Mumford stack finite and étale over Spec O_{E_Φ}, at every prime, including the primes ramified in F. It is the disjoint union of open and closed substacks M₀^{a,ξ} indexed by the classes ξ of rank-one hermitian lattices of type Φ and polarization type a. A given M₀^{a,ξ} may be empty; M₀^a is nonempty when F/F⁺ is ramified at some finite place. This extends the CM moduli of PELModuli §M4.7, which assumes p unramified in F, to every prime.
hypotheses: F/F⁺ CM, Φ a CM type, a a fractional ideal of F⁺; no condition on the residue characteristic.
proofSteps: On a local Artinian thickening, after an étale extension of the base, decompose O_F⊗O_S by places and unramified embeddings; each piece is O_S[x]/(E(x)) for an Eisenstein-type polynomial, and a quotient that is locally free with characteristic polynomial ∏_{φ∈Φ}(T−φ(π)) is R[x]/(H) with H that polynomial, so the Kottwitz condition determines the Hodge filtration.
By Grothendieck–Messing and Serre–Tate, (A₀,ι₀) and its polarization therefore deform uniquely: M₀^a is formally étale.

Properness from potentially good reduction of CM abelian varieties and finiteness of the polarized objects of fixed type; an étale proper quasi-finite Deligne–Mumford stack is finite étale. The ξ-decomposition is by the Betti lattices on complex points and descends to E_Φ.
acceptance: For F imaginary quadratic, Φ={φ} and p ramified in F, the p-divisible group of A₀ is a strict O_{F_p}-module of relative height 1, whose deformation is unique; so M₀^a is étale at p, a case excluded by the hypothesis that p is unramified in PELModuli §M4.7.

Over R=k[ε] with k of characteristic p, the x-stable submodules of R[x]/(x²) with free rank-one quotient are exactly the ideals (x+εc), c∈k, since (x+α) contains x² only when α²=0. The Kottwitz condition prescribes the characteristic polynomial T+εc of x on the quotient and so fixes c, whereas the condition rank Lie=|Φ| alone allows every c: rank conditions do not give étaleness.
Emptiness is allowed: a pair moduli problem built on M₀^{a,ξ} is empty when M₀^{a,ξ} is, and nonemptiness is a separate hypothesis wherever it is used.

nodes.statement: The localized RSZ functor is a smooth separated finite-type Deligne–Mumford stack over O_E[1/d] of relative dimension n−1. For sufficiently small levels on both the CM and unitary factors it is represented by a quasi-projective scheme, and sending a point to the product A₀×A with the action of O_F×O_F, the product polarization and the level structure induced by η₀ and η (through V(A)≅V(A₀,A)⊗V(A₀), V(A₀) being free of rank one) is a finite morphism to the PEL moduli of the product datum: the moduli of PELModuli §M2.8 when every residue characteristic of O_E[1/d] is unramified in F⁺ (then every prime of the base is good for the product datum in Lan’s sense), and otherwise the multichain moduli of gap:bad-prime-projectivity, whose multichain at every prime of the base is generated by the single self-dual lattice Λ₀⊕Λ. The theorem uses the prescribed good local types and Eisenstein condition, not just the generic Kottwitz signature.

Over O_{E,(ν)}, the semi-global functor has a CM abelian scheme (A₀,i₀,λ₀) in M₀^{a,ξ}, a unitary abelian scheme A with O_{F,(p)}-action, Kottwitz signature and Rosati quasi-polarization λ, a prime-to-p Hermitian Hom-Tate K^p-level, and at split v≠v₀ above p the specified étale Hom-level at the CM-selected factor. nodes.statement: Assume p odd, F_{v₀}/F⁺_{v₀} ramified quadratic, F⁺_{v₀}/ℚ_p unramified and Λ_{v₀} self-dual. At the distinguished rank-n factor P has structural rank n−1 and quotient conjugate rank 1; compare U5 by conjugating the local actions.

nodes.title: Exotic integral smoothness
nodes.statement: Under U7/exotic-global-model’s hypotheses and sufficiently small/neat levels, the model is smooth over O_K of relative dimension n−1. Sending a point to the product A₀×A with the action of O_F×O_F, the product polarization and the induced level structure is a finite morphism to the multichain moduli of gap:bad-prime-projectivity for the product datum, base-changed to O_K, whose multichain at u is generated by Λ₀⊕Λ_u with Λ_u π-modular (Λ_u^♯=π⁻¹Λ_u for a uniformizer π of F_u, matching ker λ[u^∞]=A[π]) and at the other places above p by the lattices of U7/exotic-global-model; hence the model is quasi-projective over O_K. It is projective in the compact Li–Liu setting F⁺≠ℚ: V is then definite at a real place, hence anisotropic, so the product datum has no cusp label and its generic fibre is proper. Changes of split prime-to-p level are finite étale. The absolute-to-relative identification used for its formal basic factor requires F⁺_u/ℚ_p unramified and is U4’s comparison.
proofSteps: Use the even-rank π-modular local-model smoothness theorem at the distinguished place.
Use the banal smooth factors and the étale CM base at the other p-places.

Prove the comparison with the product PEL moduli finite as in U7/localized-smoothness (the pair is recovered from the two idempotents of O_F×O_F; the exotic Lie and polarization conditions are closed, so the comparison is proper and quasi-finite) and pull back the quasi-projectivity of gap:bad-prime-projectivity (Stacks Tags 0B3G, 0B3H, 0C4M). For F⁺≠ℚ the generic fibre of the product datum is proper (ShimuraCompactifications §C5.5 over the reflex field, no cusp label), so the gap’s properness clause makes its moduli proper, the model is proper as it is finite over it (Stacks Tag 01WN), and proper quasi-projective is projective (Stacks Tag 0BCL). Use the prime-to-p level torsor for finite étaleness.
acceptance: Smooth relative dimension is n−1, not the absolute p-divisible-group dimension nf.
The projectivity assertion retains the compact global hypotheses.

The multichain of the comparison at u is Λ₀⊕Λ_u⊂Λ₀⊕π⁻¹Λ_u up to the periodicity by π on the second factor, so its multichain of abelian schemes is determined by A₀×A and λ; the comparison separates λ from cλ for c≠1, since λ₀×cλ is not a rational multiple of λ₀×λ.

For F⁺=ℚ and even n≥4, V of signature (n−1,1) has a trace form that is an indefinite rational quadratic form in 2n≥8 variables, isotropic by Meyer’s theorem, so V is isotropic, the product datum has a cusp label and the projectivity clause would fail; this is why it keeps F⁺≠ℚ.

nodes.title: Ramified wedge and Krämer geometry
nodes.statement: The self-dual ramified wedge model is flat, with isolated singularities; the global model is smooth away from ramified quadratic places (subject to its other local types). For every n≥2 the Krämer enhancement is regular with semistable reduction at ν when E_ν/F_{v₀} is unramified; for n≥3 it is moreover the blowup of those isolated singularities. For n=2 the wedge model itself is not regular over O_{E,ν}: its local model has reflex field F⁺_{v₀} and is semistable over O_{F⁺_{v₀}}, but E_ν contains F_{v₀}, which is ramified over F⁺_{v₀}; the Krämer local model is defined over O_{F_{v₀}} and keeps its crossing chart after an unramified extension.
proofSteps: Identify the distinguished wedge local-model factor and the trivial banal factors.
Use the explicit Krämer local-model resolution and the equal-dimension smooth chart.

Transfer the Krämer charts of U5/kramer-local-charts (étale locally yz=u times n−2 smooth parameters over O_{F̆_{v₀}}) through the local-model diagram; u stays a uniformizer over O_{Ĕ_ν} because E_ν/F_{v₀} is unramified, so the charts remain regular crossings for every n≥2. For n≥3 identify the enhancement with the blowup through the local reflex field F_{v₀}; for n=2 record that the wedge model loses semistability.
acceptance: For n≥3 the resolved relative dimension is n−1.

At n=2 the wedge local model has a chart uv=ϖ over O_{F⁺_{v₀}}; after the ramified extension with ϖ=t²·(unit) it becomes uv=t²·(unit), whose maximal ideal at u=v=t=0 needs three generators in a ring of dimension 2, so it is not regular: semistability is lost, as RSZ21 Remark 6.8 states.

At n=2 the Krämer chart yz=u lives over O_{F̆_{v₀}}; after an unramified extension E_ν/F_{v₀} the element u is still a uniformizer, so at y=z=0 the maximal ideal is generated by y and z in a ring of dimension 2: the Krämer model is regular and strictly semistable there, unlike the wedge chart of the previous Check.

nodes.title: Self-dual and almost self-dual geometry
nodes.statement: If v₀ is split in F, with self-dual Λ_{v₀} and the Eisenstein condition of U6 at the CM-selected factor w₀ (the Lubin–Tate condition of RZ17 §8, automatic when v₀ is unramified over p), the semi-global model is smooth of relative dimension n−1. If v₀ is inert, V_{v₀} is split and Λ_{v₀} self-dual, the semi-global model is smooth of relative dimension n−1; F⁺_{v₀}/ℚ_p may be ramified when the structural-action Eisenstein clause is retained. If v₀ is inert, V_{v₀} nonsplit, Λ_{v₀} almost self-dual and F⁺_{v₀}/ℚ_p unramified, the model is flat of relative dimension n−1; it is regular and semistable when E_ν/ℚ_p is unramified. At the other p-places assume the banal or permitted local types of LZ22 §11.2. For sufficiently small K^p it is representable over the CM stack by a scheme; after neat CM level it is a scheme.
proofSteps: Apply the local-model diagram, using the Eisenstein comparison on any ramified absolute base field.
Use the self-dual smooth chart or the almost self-dual semistable chart.

nodes.title: Global integral gluing and levels
nodes.statement: Under LZ22’s global lattice conditions: at 2 the CM extension is unramified; inert split V has self-dual lattice; inert nonsplit V is unramified over ℚ_p with almost self-dual lattice; split places have self-dual lattice; ramified quadratic places are unramified over ℚ_p with self-dual lattice, construct the O_E-model by integral CM pairs and all corresponding local clauses. At ramified quadratic places use the Krämer enhancement with its rank/base restrictions when a regular model is required. Introduce principal congruence levels only at split places satisfying CM matching and E_ν/E_{r,v} unramified, by normalization in the generic cover. Keep the ramified coefficient exceptions for both almost self-dual and Krämer regularity.

Identify each localization with its semi-global moduli via the canonical lattice-defined level orbit.

nodes.title: Neat smooth unitary moduli
nodes.statement: Use the special inert setting of LTXZZ22 Definition 3.3.4: p is odd, inert and unramified in F, and F⁺_𝔭=ℚ_p; take the unramified coefficient ring ℤ_{p,Φ}, N≥1, a Hermitian space V of signature (N−1,1) at the distinguished embedding and definite at the others, self-dual p-lattice and neat tame unitary/CM levels. Over the fixed finite étale CM level scheme T_p, define pairs (A₀,i₀,λ₀,η₀;A,i,λ,η^p) with A of Kottwitz type NΦ−τ∞+τ∞^c, λ p-principal, and Hermitian Hom-Tate level η^p. Arrows are prime-to-p quasi-isogenies φ₀,φ on both factors with the SAME c∈ℤ_(p)^× multiplying λ₀ and λ, and with transported CM and Hom levels. This arrow relation differs from RSZ’s exact CM-isomorphism convention and must be related through the explicit U6 quotient adapter. Sending a pair to (A₀×A, i₀×i, λ₀×λ, η₀^p⊕(η^p⊗η₀^p)), where V^p(A)≅Hom_F(V^p(A₀),V^p(A))⊗V^p(A₀) because V^p(A₀) is free of rank one, is a finite morphism to the PEL moduli of PELModuli §M2.8 for the product datum (the algebra F×F with its involution, the sum of the two Hermitian spaces, the self-dual lattice at p and a common similitude factor); p is a good prime in Lan’s sense for this datum.
proofSteps: Use the existing CM/PEL carriers with the two prescribed neat levels and special inert coefficient field.
Impose the p-principal polarization and Hom-level while using the common-scalar quasi-isogeny arrow relation on both factors.
Compare the resulting quotient to the RSZ or auxiliary-CM generic functor through the actual quotient maps.

Prove the comparison with the product PEL moduli finite: the pair is recovered from its image (A₀ and A as the images of the two idempotents of O_F×O_F, η^p from the product level structure and η₀^p), the arrow relations agree because a prime-to-p F×F-linear quasi-isogeny of A₀×A is a pair (φ₀,φ) and the PEL similitude factor is the common scalar c, and the conditions defining the source (the CM component T_p, the Kottwitz type of A, p-principality of λ) are closed; so the comparison is proper and quasi-finite, hence finite.

nodes.statement: Under the same special inert and neat coefficient hypotheses, fix the standard definite Hermitian space V° of rank N≥1 and a self-dual p-lattice; its away-p Hom-Tate data index the moduli. Define the LTXZZ22 almost self-dual CM pair with Kottwitz type NΦ−τ∞+τ∞^c and ker λ[p^∞]⊂A[p] of rank p², keeping the common p-unit scalar on both polarization arrows. At p this polarization has defect one, rather than the principal type of the fixed tame reference space. For N=1 retain the zero-dimensional smooth boundary case. The generic unitary space is a separately chosen indefinite uniformization datum, not V° itself.
proofSteps: Keep the same CM factor and arrows as in the smooth adapter.
Replace the principal local polarization condition by the rank-p² kernel bound, with the prescribed tame Hermitian reference datum.
Treat N=1 separately from the n≥2 mixed local functor.

nodes.title: Almost self-dual local equations
nodes.statement: Over a perfect residue field k of a point of T_p, the completed local ring of the almost self-dual model is either W(k)[[t₁,…,t_{N−1}]], or, for N≥2, W(k)[[x₁,…,x_N]]/(x₁x_N−p). Thus the model is regular and strictly semistable of relative dimension N−1 over the unramified coefficient ring. The N=1 model has only the first type. Quasi-projectivity does not follow from the local rings. For the uniformization datum (V′,j,Λ′_p) of U8/asd-generic-datum, sending a pair to (A₀×A, i₀×i, λ₀×λ) with the induced away-p level structure is a finite morphism to the multichain moduli of gap:bad-prime-projectivity for the product datum (the algebra F×F with its involution, V₀⊕V′, a common similitude factor), base-changed to the coefficient ring, whose multichain at p is generated by Λ₀⊕Λ′_p⊂Λ₀⊕Λ′_p^♯; hence the model is quasi-projective over T_p, and it is projective over T_p exactly when its generic fibre is proper, that is, when V′ is anisotropic. The balloon, ground and link geometry and the tangent exact sequences of Theorem 5.2.5(2)–(5) are planned by SelmerIwasawaCohomologyPartII §2.3; this target gives only the ambient local equations.
proofSteps: Normalize the local polarization pairing to diag(p,1,…,1).
Describe simultaneous Hodge line/hyperplane lifts and their orthogonality relation by Grothendieck–Messing.
In the crossing chart eliminate the remaining variables to obtain x₁x_N=p; in the other admissible charts solve for one variable to obtain a smooth power-series ring.
Check the impossible fourth rank case and the N=1 boundary before concluding semistability.

Prove the comparison with the product PEL moduli finite as in U8/ltxzz-smooth-moduli (the pair is recovered from the two idempotents of O_F×O_F and λ; the kernel condition on λ is closed). Pull back the gap’s quasi-projectivity to obtain quasi-projectivity over the coefficient ring (Stacks Tags 0B3G, 0B3H, 0C4M), hence over T_p, since the model is quasi-compact over T_p (Stacks Tag 0C4N). If the generic fibre is proper then V′ is anisotropic, the product datum has no cusp label, its generic fibre is proper (ShimuraCompactifications §C5.5 over the reflex field), the gap makes its moduli proper, the model is proper as it is finite over it (Stacks Tag 01WN), and proper quasi-projective is projective (Stacks Tag 0BCL); the converse is base change to the generic fibre.
acceptance: For N=2 the crossing ring is W(k)[[x₁,x₂]]/(x₁x₂−p).
The ambient local rings are reduced and regular although the special fibre can cross.
After a ramified coefficient extension p=t^e with e>1, this argument supplies flatness but not regularity.
For N=1, V′ has rank one and is anisotropic, so the product datum has no cusp label and the model is finite over T_p, hence projective, in agreement with its zero-dimensional boundary case.

For F⁺=ℚ and N=2, V′ has signature (1,1) and is isotropic exactly when −det V′ is a norm from F; then the product datum has a cusp label, the generic fibre is a non-proper Shimura curve and the model is quasi-projective but not projective.

The multichain of the comparison at p is Λ₀⊕Λ′_p⊂Λ₀⊕Λ′_p^♯⊂p⁻¹(Λ₀⊕Λ′_p), with Λ′_p^♯/Λ′_p of order p², so its multichain of abelian schemes is A₀×A followed by A₀×A^∨ through λ; a p-principal λ would give the single self-dual lattice of U8/ltxzz-smooth-moduli instead.

nodes.title: Integral level and Hecke system
nodes.statement: For fixed allowable integral p-type, form the system over sufficiently small prime-to-p unitary and CM compact opens. The Hecke map indexed by g in U(V)(𝔸_{F⁺,f}^p) and a in the CM torus transports η^p to η^p∘g and η₀ to η₀∘a, with the source/target compact opens satisfying the usual inclusion; correspondences are indexed by K^p\U(V)(𝔸_{F⁺,f}^p)/K′^p. The permitted level-forgetful maps are finite étale and compose compatibly. For the LTXZZ almost self-dual case use V° for the tame system and transport it through j in the generic comparison. At p only the split Drinfeld tower of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration §IG.0.31 is included.
proofSteps: Restrict the existing adelic level category to prime-to-p compact opens preserving the chosen integral local type.
Transport the two level structures on the same polarized abelian pair and verify the common-scalar arrow equivalence.
Use the prime-to-p étale Tate torsors to prove finite étaleness, and compare the generic Hecke composition with the imported level category.

nodes.title: Mixed integral isogeny moduli
nodes.statement: At the inert almost self-dual distinguished place v₀, choose the totally positive global scalar u₀=(x₀,x₀)∈F⁺ with valuation one at v₀ and zero at the other v|p, and the rank-(n+1) Hermitian extension V♯=V⊥⟨u₀⟩ with the lattices and compact opens of LZ22 §13.4. Enhance the semi-global CM pair by a principal-at-v₀ target A♯ and an O_{F,(p)}-linear isogeny α:A×A₀→A♯ in the prime-to-p isogeny category, with ker α⊂(A×A₀)[u₀], α*λ♯=λ×u₀λ₀, and transported tame and other-p levels. Fix the selected CM component and framing isogeny. The v₀-primary degree is q²: the two source polarization factors each have degree q² there, and the target is principal there. Any degree statement for an actual global representative must also retain its away-p factors. The printed global degree q is incompatible with this necessary local equation. Conjugating the global signature (n−1,1) to U1’s (1,n−1) sends the local CM source to ℰ̄ of U2.
proofSteps: Choose V♯, u₀, the local self-dual overlattice and the other levels exactly as in §13.4; impose the isogeny relation in the localized abelian-scheme category.
Impose the displayed polarization pullback and transported levels; derive its degree rather than the incompatible printed degree.
Fix the basic framing component so that its distinguished deformation problem is the mixed local functor.

nodes.title: Smooth integral geometry and tangent space
nodes.statement: The neat smooth unitary model is a smooth quasi-projective scheme over T_p of relative dimension N−1. At a geometric point its relative tangent space is Hom(ω_{A∨,τ∞},H₁^dR(A)_{τ∞}/ω_{A∨,τ∞}), with source rank 1 and target rank N−1. Its generic fibre is the canonical unitary Shimura variety times the CM factor. It is projective over T_p exactly when its generic fibre is proper. Both quasi-projectivity and this criterion come from the PEL moduli of the product A₀×A through the finite comparison morphism of U8/ltxzz-smooth-moduli: that PEL moduli is quasi-projective (ShimuraCompactifications §C5.18); the product datum has a cusp label exactly when the product Hermitian space has a nonzero totally isotropic F×F-stable subspace, that is, the CM line being anisotropic, exactly when V is isotropic, which is exactly when the generic fibre is not proper; with no cusp label the PEL moduli is proper (ShimuraCompactifications §C5.5). Projectivity does not follow from smoothness and quasi-projectivity alone. Here H₁^dR is the dual of the imported H¹_dR. On complex points the negative period line is Hom_ℂ(H₁^dR(A₀)_{τ∞},ω_{A∨,τ∞}); the condition on the zero subspace ω_{A₀∨,τ∞} cannot define that line.
proofSteps: Compute the polarized Hodge deformation using the rank-one distinguished quotient; the other factors are banal.

Use neat levels for scheme representability; for quasi-projectivity pull back the quasi-projectivity of ShimuraCompactifications §C5.18 along the finite comparison of U8/ltxzz-smooth-moduli (a finite morphism is quasi-affine of finite type, hence quasi-projective, and quasi-projective morphisms compose over a quasi-compact base and are stable under base change: Stacks Tags 0B3H, 0C4M, 0B3G); this gives quasi-projectivity over the coefficient ring, and over T_p because the model is quasi-compact over T_p (Stacks Tag 0C4N).

Identify the generic canonical model. For the projectivity clause: if the generic fibre is proper then V is anisotropic, the product datum has no cusp label, its PEL moduli is proper by ShimuraCompactifications §C5.5, the model is proper as it is finite over that moduli (Stacks Tag 01WN), and a proper quasi-projective morphism is projective (Stacks Tag 0BCL); the converse is base change to the generic fibre.
acceptance: For N=2 the tangent dimension is one.
The CM tangent contribution is zero because T_p is étale over the coefficient ring.

For F⁺=ℚ and N=2, V has signature (1,1) and is isotropic exactly when −det V is a norm from F; then the product datum has a cusp label, the generic fibre is a non-proper Shimura curve and the model is not projective, while for anisotropic V the model is projective.

nodes.title: Tate–Dieudonné comparison for basic CM pairs
nodes.statement: Let A and A′ be polarized abelian varieties over F̄_p and K a commutative semisimple ℚ-algebra acting on both through embeddings into the rational endomorphism algebras that are stable under the Rosati involutions, such that for every place 𝔭 of K above p the 𝔭-parts N_𝔭 and N′_𝔭 of the two rational Dieudonné modules are isoclinic of the same slope; equivalently, A×A′ with the diagonal K-action and the product polarization has isoclinic 𝔭-part at every 𝔭. Then Hom_K(A,A′)⊗ℚ_ℓ→Hom_K(V_ℓA,V_ℓA′) is an isomorphism for every prime ℓ≠p, and Hom_K(A,A′)⊗ℚ_p is isomorphic to the K-linear maps of rational Dieudonné modules commuting with Frobenius. A unitary CM pair (A₀,A) of this roadmap (K=F) is basic when A₀×A satisfies this hypothesis: at a place w of F above p other than the distinguished one, A[w^∞] is isogenous to the n-th power of a rank-one O_{F_w}-module and both A₀[w^∞] and A[w^∞] have slope |Φ_w|/[F_w:ℚ_p], where Φ_w is the set of embeddings in Φ inducing w; at the distinguished place, inert or ramified over F⁺ in the uniformizations of this layer, basicness means that A[w^∞] is isoclinic, hence of slope 1/2 like A₀[w^∞]. For a basic pair this identifies Hom_{O_F}(A₀,A)⊗ℚ_v with the local Hom spaces at every finite place v of F⁺, compatibly with the hermitian forms, and the group of polarized self-quasi-isogenies of the pair with an inner form of the RSZ group.
hypotheses: K, A, A′ as stated; at every place 𝔭 of K above p, N_𝔭 and N′_𝔭 are isoclinic of the same slope (each factor being isoclinic separately does not suffice).
proofSteps: Apply RZ96 Lemma 6.28 to A×A′ with the diagonal K-action and the product polarization, whose hypothesis is the common-slope condition: over a large enough finite field, over which A, A′ and all K-linear homomorphisms are defined, a power of the Frobenius of A×A′ is the image of one element u∈K acting diagonally.

Away from p apply Tate’s theorem over finite fields (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison §8.3) to A×A′ and take the K-linear corner Hom_K(A,A′); since the same u gives the Frobenius power of both factors, every K-linear map V_ℓA→V_ℓA′ intertwines the two Frobenius powers.

At p use the Dieudonné-module form of Tate’s theorem over the finite field for A×A′, proved by the same commutant and dimension count and restricted to the same corner, with the isogeny classification of FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory §R07.2.17 and the B-linear classification of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison §8.10.
acceptance: For a supersingular elliptic curve A=A′ and K=ℚ both sides at ℓ≠p have dimension 4 (End⁰A⊗ℚ_ℓ=M₂(ℚ_ℓ)), and at p both are the quaternion division algebra over ℚ_p of invariant 1/2, the endomorphisms of the isoclinic slope-1/2 isocrystal of height 2.
The isoclinic hypothesis is necessary: for an ordinary elliptic curve over F̄_p and K=ℚ, End⁰ is an imaginary quadratic field of dimension 2 while End(V_ℓ) has dimension 4.

Each factor being isoclinic at every place does not suffice: for K imaginary quadratic with p split, A an ordinary elliptic curve over F̄_p with CM by O_K and A′=A with the K-action precomposed by conjugation, every 𝔭-part is one-dimensional, hence isoclinic, but at 𝔭 the slopes are 0 and 1. Hom_K(A,A′)=0, since End⁰A=K is commutative and fι(a)=ι(ā)f forces (a−ā)f=0, while the conjugate-semilinear maps of the free rank-one K⊗ℚ_ℓ-module V_ℓA form a ℚ_ℓ-space of dimension 2; at p both sides vanish.
For a basic pair with V_ℓA₀ free of rank one and V_ℓA free of rank n over F⊗ℚ_ℓ, Hom_F has rank n over F⊗ℚ_ℓ, matching dim_F Hom_{O_F}(A₀,A)⊗ℚ=n.

nodes.title: Quotients of formal schemes by discrete groups
nodes.statement: Let 𝔐 be a formal scheme locally formally of finite type over Spf O_Ĕ and Γ a group acting on 𝔐 over Spf O_Ĕ such that (i) every quasi-compact open subset of 𝔐_red meets only finitely many of its Γ-translates and (ii) every point of 𝔐 has an open neighbourhood U with γU∩U=∅ for every γ≠1 in Γ; in particular Γ acts freely on all points of 𝔐_red, generic points of components included. Construct the quotient Γ\𝔐: the fpqc quotient sheaf is represented by a formal scheme locally formally of finite type over Spf O_Ĕ and 𝔐→Γ\𝔐 is a Γ-torsor and a local isomorphism. Hypothesis (ii) is what makes the quotient a formal scheme rather than the formal algebraic space of RZ96 Proposition 2.37: Γ\𝔐 is then locally isomorphic to 𝔐. For the unitary uniformization data of U9 — the group I(ℚ) of polarized self-quasi-isogenies of a basic pair, acting on 𝔐×G(𝔸_f^p)/K^p — conditions (i) and (ii) hold when K^p is small enough that every intersection of I(ℚ) with a conjugate of J(ℚ_p)×K^p is torsion free, as in RZ96 Theorem 6.30; for general K^p the quotient is a formal Deligne–Mumford stack with finite stabilizers. The quotient is used as a sheaf on Nilp_{O_Ĕ}, not only through its geometric points.
hypotheses: 𝔐, Γ as stated; for the unitary application K^p sufficiently small as stated.
proofSteps: Choose a covering of 𝔐 by opens U with U∩γU=∅ for γ≠1, as (ii) allows.
Glue the images of these opens along the Γ-action to obtain Γ\𝔐, and check that it represents the quotient sheaf.

For the unitary application, use that I(ℚ) is discrete in J(ℚ_p)×G(𝔸_f^p) (proof of RZ96 Theorem 6.23) and that the stabilizers in J(ℚ_p) of points and of irreducible components of 𝔐_red are compact, so stabilizers in I(ℚ) are finite and trivial when the stated intersections are torsion free; local finiteness follows from discreteness in the same way (RZ96 Proposition 2.34).

nodes.title: Krämer completion compatibility
nodes.statement: For every n≥2, in the ramified setting of U7/ramified-kramer-model with E_ν/F_{v₀} unramified, the global Krämer enhancement completed along a selected basic component is the corresponding principal ramified framed completion with the U5 Krämer filtration, times its CM and other discrete local factors and modulo the global framing group. The comparison conjugates the local Lie labels as specified in U7 and preserves the forgetful map to the wedge model. It uses the moduli functor and Θ, not the regularity of either side.
proofSteps: Apply the formal deformation comparison to the underlying polarized ramified pair.
Transport the Hodge filtration to the precisely labeled Krämer subbundle through the local-model diagram.
Check descent of the enhancement and compatibility with the wedge forgetful maps.
acceptance: The completed subbundle has rank n−1 with the declared local conjugate action.

At n=2 the comparison is asserted as for n≥3: both sides are étale locally yz=u over O_{Ĕ_ν} (U5/kramer-local-charts), and nothing in the comparison uses the blowup description of RSZ21 Theorem 6.7(ii), which needs n≥3.

nodes.title: Mixed basic-locus comparison
nodes.statement: The completion of the corrected mixed integral isogeny model at its chosen basic framing component is the arithmetic quotient of the mixed local framed space Ñ¹_n with the same CM, other-p and tame factors as in U9. The two forgetful maps to the almost self-dual and principal rank-(n+1) completions correspond to π₁ and π₂ of U2, equivariantly for the embedded nearby group. On generic fibres they recover the stated isogeny correspondence. Its proof uses the moduli functor and generic projections. For context, LRZ26 Theorem 14.6.2 proves that π₁ is integrally finite flat of degree q+1 and π₂ is proper and an isomorphism away from a zero-dimensional center, with exceptional projective spaces. There is no integral identification Ñ¹_n≅Z(x₀). That divisor-resolution and its intersection consequences belong to the cycle consumer, rather than being a hypothesis of this moduli uniformization.
proofSteps: Use Serre–Tate full faithfulness for the finite-kernel isogeny α as well as its source and target.
Identify the local framing isogeny and the two transported level structures.
Apply Θ to the enhanced functor and verify that forgetting α commutes with both quotient maps.
acceptance: The local isogeny has degree q² consistent with the polarization identity.
The first generic projection has degree q+1; this is not the degree of α.

gaps.title: Displays of formal p-divisible groups over nilpotent bases
gaps.detail: PELModuli §M2.15 defines Zink displays and the functor BT, and states the equivalence only over complete local noetherian rings with perfect residue field. Mih19 §11.2, p. 43, recalls the equivalence over every ring in which p is nilpotent, on which the O-display theory of U0 rests.
gaps.needs: For every ring R in which p is nilpotent, prove that BT is an equivalence from nilpotent displays over R to formal p-divisible groups over R, compatible with base change and with duality of biformal objects.

gaps.title: Global hermitian spaces with prescribed local invariants
gaps.detail: GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic §§2.7 and 2.9 classify local hermitian lattices and forms, and PELModuli §§M3.1–M3.2 give the forms of a unitary datum and the Hasse principle. No roadmap states the existence of a global hermitian space with prescribed real signatures and finite invariants; SelmerIwasawaCohomologyPartII declares the same contract.
gaps.needs: For a CM extension F/F⁺, prove that a global F/F⁺-hermitian space with prescribed real signatures and finite local invariants exists exactly when the invariants satisfy the product formula, and is unique up to isometry.

gaps.title: Smoothness of polarized unitary multichain automorphism schemes
gaps.detail: ReductiveGroupsPartII §RG2.3.5 (lattice-chain-stabilizer-schemes) treats GL and GSp chains only; the RSZ local-model diagram needs the trivialization torsor of a polarized O_F-multichain.
gaps.needs: For p>2, a quadratic extension of p-adic fields and a polarized periodic lattice multichain, prove its automorphism group scheme smooth, including the Weil-restricted factors when the ground field is ramified over ℚ_p, and identify it with the corresponding stabilizer group scheme.

gaps.title: Quasi-projectivity and properness of PEL models at bad primes and parahoric levels
gaps.detail: ShimuraCompactifications §§C5.5 and C5.18 prove properness and quasi-projectivity of PEL moduli over a base of good primes in Lan’s sense, and PELModuli §§M1.7 and M2.8 define and represent the PEL moduli only over such a base; U8/smooth-geometry-tangent, and U7/localized-smoothness on a base of good primes, consume Layer C5 directly. This contract asks for the moduli problem itself at the remaining primes, in the multichain formulation of RZ96 Definition 6.9, and for its representability, quasi-projectivity and properness; U7/localized-smoothness on a base with a bad prime, U7/exotic-global-smoothness and U8/asd-completed-local-rings reach it through finite comparison morphisms from their CM-pair models for the product datum A₀×A.
gaps.needs: Pose the PEL moduli problem of PELModuli §M1.7 (Lan, Definition 1.4.1.4) over an integral base, a localization of the ring of integers of the reflex field or the ring of integers of one of its completions, that contains primes at which ShimuraCompactifications Layer C5 does not apply (primes dividing the discriminant of the PEL order, or primes whose local level is not the stabilizer of a single self-dual lattice), replacing the abelian scheme at each such prime by a multichain of abelian schemes indexed by a polarized lattice multichain of the PEL order and taking the level there to be the stabilizer of that multichain, as in RZ96 Definition 6.9, p. 279; prove that this moduli problem is represented by a separated Deligne–Mumford stack of finite type over the base, at neat level by a quasi-projective scheme through an ample Hodge line, and that it is proper over the base when its generic fibre is proper.

sourceIssues.printed: The framing condition specifies a height-zero O_L-linear quasi-isogeny without relating the two polarizations.
sourceIssues.correction: Require its pullback of the framing polarization to be locally an O_K-unit multiple of the object polarization, and use polarization-compatible arrows.
sourceIssues.reason: The framed Hermitian isocrystal and its lattice pairing are not fixed by O_L-linearity and height alone. Howard19 §2 imposes the missing compatibility, which is used to identify the lattice moduli.

sourceIssues.printed: The introductory description gives the Krämer filtration rank one.
sourceIssues.correction: In signature (1,n−1), use a rank-(n−1) conjugate-character subbundle and a rank-one structural-character quotient.
sourceIssues.reason: Definition 2.2(3) and the Lie decomposition have that rank; the introductory rank agrees only when n=2.

sourceIssues.printed: The unitary Hecke parameter is written using adeles of F rather than of F⁺.
sourceIssues.correction: Use U(V)(𝔸_{F⁺}^{∞,p}) and the corresponding unitary double cosets.
sourceIssues.reason: U(V) is a group over F⁺; extension to the CM-field adeles changes its points to a different group. Definition 3.1.11 and the surrounding level data fix the intended base.

sourceIssues.locator: Theorem 4.2.3, last assertion and proof, published p. 161
sourceIssues.printed: The theorem identifies projectivity of the integral model with projectivity of its generic fibre, while the displayed proof treats representability and tangent spaces.
sourceIssues.correction: Add a valuative or flat-boundary proof of integral properness under proper generic fibre, then use the ample Hodge bundle for projectivity; at the special inert prime of the theorem this is ShimuraCompactifications §§C5.5 and C5.18 transported along the finite comparison with the PEL moduli of the product A₀×A (U8/ltxzz-smooth-moduli, U8/smooth-geometry-tangent).
sourceIssues.reason: A smooth quasi-projective model with proper generic fibre need not be proper. RSZ21 Theorem 4.4 supplies the representability/smoothness input, but is not a replacement for the missing integral properness argument.

sourceIssues.printed: The auxiliary global isogeny is assigned degree q alongside the product pullback-polarization equation.
sourceIssues.correction: The necessary v₀-primary degree is q², with q=#k_{F⁺,v₀}; the degree of an actual global representative also includes any away-p factors. Distinguish it from the degree q+1 of the first mixed projection.
sourceIssues.reason: Locally at v₀ both source polarization factors have degree q² and the target is principal, so (deg α_{v₀})²=q⁴. In particular a global isogeny of degree q cannot satisfy the equation. For q=3 its required v₀-primary degree is 9.

sourceIssues.locator: §4.3, p. 58, and §4.5, p. 66, author copy dated 16 January 2022
sourceIssues.printed: The exotic conditions at ramified p-places are applied to the CM source A₀[v^∞], including A₀[u^∞] at the distinguished place.
sourceIssues.correction: Apply the rank-n exotic condition to A[v^∞] (and to A[u^∞] at the distinguished place); the source is the separately specified principal rank-one CM object.
sourceIssues.reason: The target has the required absolute height 2nf and mixed signature; the CM source has height 2f and cannot satisfy the rank-n exotic condition for even n≥2.

sourceIssues.printed: The proposed negative period line is defined by requiring a Hom map to send the source Hodge subspace into the target Hodge subspace.
sourceIssues.correction: At τ∞ use Hom_ℂ(H₁^dR(A₀)_{τ∞},ω_{A∨,τ∞}) inside the corresponding Hom realization.
sourceIssues.reason: The source Hodge subspace at τ∞ has rank zero, so the printed condition is vacuous. For N>1 it defines the full N-dimensional Hom space instead of the rank-one period line.

sourceIssues.printed: The ℓ-adic and p-adic K-linear Hom comparisons are asserted for any two polarized K-objects each of which satisfies the isoclinic hypothesis of Lemma 6.28 separately.
sourceIssues.correction: Require that at every place of K above p the two 𝔭-parts be isoclinic of the same slope, so that Lemma 6.28 applied to A×A′ gives one element of K inducing a Frobenius power on both factors; the comparisons then follow from Tate’s theorem on the K-linear corner of End(A×A′).
sourceIssues.reason: For K imaginary quadratic with p split, an ordinary CM elliptic curve A and A′=A with conjugated K-action, each object satisfies the separate hypothesis, yet Hom_K(A,A′)⊗ℚ_ℓ=0 while Hom_K(V_ℓA,V_ℓA′) has dimension 2 (U9/basic-hom-comparison).
